title: South America mined lithium supply to grow 77% by 2040
gist: Benchmark's Lithium Service forecasts South American mined lithium supply rising 77% from 444kt LCE in 2026 to 784kt in 2040, led by Argentina growing from 111kt to 337kt while Chile grows 25% from 296kt to 371kt.

insights.claim: Benchmark's Lithium Service expects South American mined lithium supply to grow 77% from 444kt LCE in 2026 to 784kt in 2040.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sets the regional supply baseline against which lithium price and project-timing views can be tested.
insights.locator: South America’s supply of mined lithium

insights.claim: The 77% regional growth to 2040 is driven largely by Argentina rather than Chile.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Marginal supply growth is concentrated in one jurisdiction, so Argentine policy and execution matter most.
insights.locator: This growth is driven in large part by Argentina

insights.claim: Argentina's lithium supply is forecast to rise more than 200%, from 111kt to 337kt, between 2026 and 2040, while Chile grows 25% from 296kt to 371kt, so Argentina largely catches up with Chile.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Watch Argentine developers as the main source of incremental supply and Chilean producers as slower-growth incumbents.
insights.locator: Argentina’s supply is expected to increase

insights.claim: Benchmark analyst Federico Gay says Argentina has become a beacon for lithium investment because of high-quality resources and a favourable investment framework that raises companies' appetite to commit capital.
insights.speaker: Federico Gay
insights.so_what: Supportive investment rules are a key driver of capital flowing to Argentine lithium projects.
insights.quote: Argentina has become a beacon for lithium investment, driven by a combination of high-quality resources and a favourable investment framework

insights.claim: Argentina is bringing lithium projects online quickly and still has a very attractive development pipeline, according to Federico Gay.
insights.speaker: Federico Gay
insights.so_what: A deep pipeline implies continued supply additions beyond projects already operating.
insights.locator: The country is bringing projects online quickly
